metadata.title: Technical SEO Audit with AISO Checks (Lite)
metadata.description: Technical SEO audit with AISO-specific checks -- crawlability, indexability, security, URL structure, mobile-friendliness, and AI crawler access. Requires explicit audit_scope declaration in every output. Reports checks passed per category, not a numeric score. Lite edition for workshop use.

changelog.1.1: Added mandatory audit_scope field (homepage_only | representative_templates | full_site_crawl). Every output must declare scope in header to prevent client misinterpretation of findings as site-wide. Added detection_logic for auto-selecting scope from user prompt.
changelog.1.1-lite: Workshop edition. Five categories, no point weighting. Results are reported as checks passed per category.

metadata.author: RAINMOJO SO

configuration.purpose: Audit 5 categories of technical health with specific attention to AISO requirements, most critically AI crawler access.

audit_scope.enforcement: MANDATORY. The skill MUST ask the user or detect scope before starting the audit, and MUST state scope prominently at the top of the output (first H2 section, in a callout box).

homepage_only.description: Audit ONLY the single URL provided (typically the homepage). Fastest. Cheapest. Least representative.
homepage_only.when_to_use: User provides a single URL with no sitemap access · Quick preliminary check · Pitch/proposal context · Free trial tier
homepage_only.output_disclaimer: SCOPE NOTE: This audit covers ONLY the homepage ({url}). Findings may not represent site-wide patterns. Template-specific issues (event pages, category pages, programmatic pages) are NOT evaluated. For full-site readiness, re-run with audit_scope=representative_templates or full_site_crawl.

representative_templates.description: Audit homepage + 1 sample of each major template type (listing page, detail page, category page, article page, programmatic page if applicable)
representative_templates.when_to_use: Standard client audit · Dynamic site with multiple page types (event platform, marketplace, news, ecommerce, directory)
representative_templates.output_disclaimer: SCOPE NOTE: This audit covers {N} representative pages across {M} template types: {template_list}. Findings apply to each audited template type; pages not matching these templates may differ. Individual page variations (e.g. specific events, products) are NOT audited, only the template.

full_site_crawl.description: Crawl sitemap.xml and audit all unique URL patterns up to configured limit
full_site_crawl.when_to_use: Comprehensive enterprise audit · Post-migration verification · Monthly re-audit · Compliance review
full_site_crawl.output_disclaimer: SCOPE NOTE: This audit covers {N} pages discovered via sitemap crawl (crawl_limit={limit}). Pages blocked by robots.txt or missing from sitemap are NOT audited. Findings are statistically representative but not exhaustive.
full_site_crawl.requires: sitemap.xml access or explicit list of URLs

detection_logic: If user provides single URL and no sitemap reference, prompt: 'Audit scope? (1) Homepage-only [fast, 3 min] (2) Representative templates [balanced, 12 min] (3) Full site crawl [thorough, 45 min]'
If user mentions specific page types (e.g. 'event pages', 'category pages', 'blog articles'), default to representative_templates and ask which template types to sample
If user says 'full site', 'entire site', 'ทุกหน้า', 'ทั้งเว็บ', use full_site_crawl
If user says 'quick check', 'เช็คเร็วๆ', 'homepage', use homepage_only

workflow.purpose: Technical SEO forms the foundation of both traditional search and AI search citation. This audits 5 categories with specific attention to AISO requirements, above all AI crawler access.
pre_audit_steps: STEP 0A (required): ทำขั้นที่ 0 ใน SKILL.md ก่อน คือดึง HTML ดิบ response header และ robots.txt ลง work/{domain}/uploads/ แล้วตรวจจากไฟล์เหล่านั้น ห้ามตรวจ canonical, meta robots, viewport, mixed content และ security header จากผล WebFetch เพราะถูกตัดทิ้ง
STEP 0B (required): Declare audit_scope. Prompt user if ambiguous. Record in metadata.

STEP 0C (required for any rendering finding): capture the three JavaScript-visibility tiers described in SKILL.md before writing any SSR, rendering, or cloaking finding. Tier 1 is the raw no-JS fetch from STEP 0A. Tiers 2 and 3 cannot be captured with curl or WebFetch: ask the user for the DevTools outerHTML copies. If they are unavailable, record ตรวจไม่ได้ for every check that needs them and never record ไม่มี.
STEP 1: If full_site_crawl, fetch sitemap.xml and derive URL list. If representative_templates, identify template types from sitemap patterns or ask user.

checks.robotstxt_validity: Fetch robots.txt. Check syntax. Verify sitemap referenced.

ai_crawler_access.description: CRITICAL for AISO. Check robots.txt for all AI crawler directives.

crawlers.Google-Extended: Gemini/Google AI training (does NOT affect search rankings)

ai_crawler_access.result: Pass if every listed crawler is allowed. Fail if any of Googlebot, bingbot, GPTBot, PerplexityBot or ClaudeBot is blocked, and list which ones. ถ้าดึง robots.txt ไม่สำเร็จ ให้เขียนว่า ตรวจไม่ได้ ห้ามเขียนว่าถูกบล็อกและห้ามเขียนว่าผ่าน

checks.xml_sitemaps: Fetch sitemap. Validate XML. Check lastmod dates. Count URLs. Verify status codes.
checks.crawl_depth: All important pages within 3 clicks of homepage.
checks.noindex_management: Check for erroneous noindex on indexable pages.

checks.canonical_tags: Every page must have self-referencing canonical. Check for conflicts and chains.
checks.duplicate_content: www vs non-www, HTTP vs HTTPS, trailing slashes, parameter duplicates. Detecting WHICH urls duplicate each other belongs to technical-audit-lite; this skill owns the ORDER of the remedies. See duplicate_remedy_ladder below and state that ordering in the report.
checks.pagination: Plain crawlable links between paginated pages, or one view-all page with a canonical from every paginated URL to it. Do not rely on rel=next/prev: the major engine retired it, so it is an inert instruction rather than a pagination mechanism.
checks.hreflang: Reciprocal hreflang, x-default fallback, valid language/region codes.
checks.index_bloat: Indexed pages vs actual valuable content.

checks.https: HTTPS enforced. HTTP redirects to HTTPS. No mixed content. Valid cert.

checks.clean_urls: Human-readable, no session IDs, lowercase, hyphens, no special chars.
checks.redirect_chains: Max 1 hop. No loops. Classify by code rather than by a blanket rule: 301 and 308 are permanent; 302, 303 and 307 are temporary. The defect is a PERMANENT move served with a temporary code, because the old URL can stay indexed and keep the authority. A temporary code is correct for genuinely temporary routing such as geo or locale routing, maintenance, and checkout. Also flag any redirect that answers 200 or 404, and any meta refresh with a delay above zero, as separate defects.
checks.parameter_handling: No duplicate indexable pages from params.

category_5_mobile.context: As of July 2024, Google crawls ALL sites exclusively with mobile Googlebot.

checks.responsive_design: Viewport meta tag. No horizontal scrolling. No fixed-width layouts.
checks.content_parity: All desktop content visible on mobile.

js_visibility_tiers.rule: Diagnose JavaScript visibility from THREE captures of the same URL, never from a raw-versus-rendered pair. A two-snapshot check cannot separate content a rendering crawler will reach from content no crawler will ever reach, and those two findings have different remedies.

tiers.tier_1_raw_html_no_js: The response body as delivered, with no JavaScript executed. Exactly what a crawler that does not render receives.
tiers.tier_2_initial_rendered_dom: The DOM after the initial JavaScript settles, with the page untouched. What a rendering crawler receives in one pass.
tiers.tier_3_post_interaction_dom: The DOM after opening a dropdown, clicking a tab, or pressing load-more. What a human sees. No crawler reaches this state.

js_visibility_tiers.banned_source: Browser view-source counts as tier 1 only. Never use it to answer the tier 2 or tier 3 question, because it shows the script rather than the rendered result.

classification.present_in_tier_2_absent_from_tier_1: Invisible to crawlers that do not render. Remedy family: rendering strategy, move the content into the server response.
classification.present_in_tier_3_absent_from_tier_2: Invisible to EVERY crawler regardless of rendering ability, because no crawler clicks. Remedy family: link architecture. A rendering change does nothing for this class.

interaction_gated_content.rule: Interaction-gated content is its own finding class, not a rendering defect. It is absent from the crawl even on a fully rendering crawler.
interaction_gated_content.remedy: Each block needs either its own URL or a crawlable link path. Apply the same rule to state swapped in at one URL, where only the default state is indexed.
interaction_gated_content.legitimate_inverse: Leaving filter and sort permutations behind interaction is a valid way to keep them out of the crawl. Record it as an intentional and correct choice, never as a defect.

uncrawlable_link_constructs.classification: Report under LINK-ARCHITECTURE, never under rendering, because the fix is markup rather than a rendering strategy.

constructs.non_anchor_navigation: Navigation built from non-anchor elements with script click handlers instead of anchor elements with an href. Remedy: a real <a href> to the destination URL, with script layered on top if wanted.
constructs.fragment_only_urls: URLs that differ from one another only by a fragment identifier. Remedy: give each destination a distinct path that stands on its own.

uncrawlable_link_constructs.why_it_matters: Both are permitted by frameworks and both produce zero crawlable link graph even when the page renders perfectly, so the pages behind them are undiscoverable. A clean tier 1 versus tier 2 diff does not clear a site of this defect.

cloaking_boundary.allowed: Serving a server-rendered version to crawlers and a client-rendered one to users is acceptable provided the two are substantially the same content.
cloaking_regardless_of_stated_intent: Content hidden with a display-none rule specifically to feed engines
Content that exists only inside a noscript block
Content swapped by IP or user agent
cloaking_boundary.false_positive_guard: The divergence that arises naturally from client-side rendering is normally NOT cloaking. Report it as a rendering-dependency risk, never as a cloaking violation. Escalate only when the divergence is server-side AND conditioned on the requesting agent. Without this guard an SSR/CSR check that finds source HTML differing from rendered HTML escalates a normal single-page application into a cloaking accusation in a client report.

render_latency.rule: Pages needing a render pass wait in a deferred queue; fully server-rendered pages skip it. Treat this as an indexing-LATENCY risk, not only a visibility risk.
render_latency.operational_rule: Any field whose accuracy is time-sensitive must be present in the server HTML: price, availability, event date, breaking content. Tell a client-rendered site that new and changed content is indexed on a lag it does not control.
render_latency.no_numbers: Never state a queue wait in seconds or minutes. This edition ships no measured latency figures and must not invent one.

duplicate_remedy_ladder.rule: The four duplicate remedies are ORDERED, not interchangeable. Work down from rung 1 and drop a rung only when the one above is genuinely impossible for this client. A report that lists them as options of equal standing is defective.
rungs: 1. Eliminate the duplicate URL at source so one URL serves the content, with a 301 from every retired URL to the survivor. The 301 is the only rung that carries each retired URL accumulated authority to the survivor. Cost: a change at the source of the duplication, not just a tag.
2. Canonical. It is a suggestion the engine may override, but it keeps the duplicate reachable and separately measurable in analytics, unlike a 301, which moves humans too.

4. robots.txt Disallow, LAST for duplicates specifically, on three counts: an uncrawled duplicate still consumes discovery, it still strands any links pointing at it, and its signals cannot be consolidated into the survivor.
duplicate_remedy_ladder.reporting_rule: State the ordering explicitly whenever a robots block is proposed, or is already in place, for a duplicate. The robots block is the easiest option and therefore the one a run reaches for.
duplicate_remedy_ladder.handoff: Detecting which URLs are duplicates belongs to technical-audit-lite. The robots.txt deploy file belongs to aiso-crawlers-lite.

indexnow_protocol.description: Open protocol for instant search engine notification. Supported by Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver. ChatGPT uses Bing's index, so faster Bing indexing means faster AI visibility.
indexnow_protocol.check: Look for key file at /.well-known/indexnow-key.txt or CMS plugin.

overall_result.method: ไม่มีคะแนนรวม รายงานเป็นจำนวนข้อที่ผ่านต่อจำนวนข้อทั้งหมดในแต่ละหมวด เช่น Crawlability 4/5
overall_result.reporting_rule: List every failed check by name with the fix. Do not convert the counts into a percentage or a grade. ข้อที่ดึงข้อมูลไม่สำเร็จให้แยกไว้เป็น ตรวจไม่ได้ ห้ามนับรวมเป็นข้อที่ผ่านและห้ามนับรวมเป็นข้อที่ตก และตรวจได้ไม่ครบทุกหมวดก็ยังต้องส่งหมวดที่ตรวจได้
overall_result.rendering_finding_rules: Record which TIER each missing item sits in; a finding that says only missing from raw HTML collapses two defects that need different remedies. Never write cloaking merely because source HTML differs from rendered HTML. Never propose a robots.txt block for a duplicate without stating that it is the bottom rung and why.
overall_result.scope_adjusted_reporting: Under homepage_only scope, the counts describe only the audited page. A homepage-only result does NOT describe the whole site, it describes the homepage. State this explicitly in the output.

output.required_header: Section 1 MUST be 'Audit Scope' using output_header_template
sections: Audit Scope (scope mode + disclaimer + pages audited)
Checks Passed by Category table (passed / total per category)
AI Crawler Access table (all crawlers with status and recommendation)
JavaScript Visibility by Tier (which tier each missing item sits in, plus interaction-gated blocks and uncrawlable link constructs)
Duplicate URL Remedies (proposed rung per duplicate set, with the ladder ordering stated)
Pages NOT Audited (disclaimer section listing what was excluded from scope)
